A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fecal indicator bacteria are a useful tool for assessing the potential for fecal pollution in tidally mixed estuaries.

fecal indicator bacteria are not a useful tool for identifying the sources of fecal pollution in tidally mixed waters, such as Newport Bay, because of the complex and dynamic nature of the transport pathways that govern their distribution in the water column.
fecal indicator bacteria concentrations are elevated in the water column of Newport Bay, and that this impairment is primarily caused by nonpoint sources of dry weather and storm runoff.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the water quality of a tidally mixed coastal estuary is not a simple function of its immediate watershed, but also a function of the watershed of its watershed.

, while the water quality in Newport Bay is generally quite good, the water column and sediments can become contaminated by fecal indicator bacteria, and this contamination is likely to occur more frequently during periods of higher flow, such as storm events.

fecal indicator bacteria concentrations can be highly variable in time and space, and that this variability must be understood and accounted for when designing and interpreting studies that seek to identify and quantify fecal indicator bacteria sources and transport pathways.
